tone_statements.citation: Foley, Sean & Dylan Elliott. 2022. Revisiting Central Ngwi tones: a computational approach. Poster presented at the Annual Meeting of the Linguistic Society of America, Washington, D.C., January 6-9, 2022. 1 p. (University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill).
tone_statements.quote: • Lexical data collected from 23 Ngwi languages, 21 grouped into CN and one language from Southern and Northern Ngwi for comparison (1) [...] • ~130 cognate sets extracted from which tone-onset correspondences were established • Applying the Tonal Comparative Method (TCM) (Dockum 2019), toneonset correspondences used to establish any shared tone changes • Python used to sort through tone-onset correspondences to ascertain shared tone changes across the 21 CN languages [...] Taloid Talu, Lavu (Chen 2010); Kuansi (Castro, Flaming & Crook 2010); Naruo (Foley 2020); Tagu (Yang, et al. 2017); [...] Patterns evident from the data: 1. Original PN tone values most prevalent across reflexes of all five tones 2. Not all of the languages share the proposed tone changes for CN 3. No consistent tone changes shared among all of the proposed CN languages

tone_statements.citation: Foley, Sean. 2020. Naruo: an endangered Ngwi language spoken in Yunnan, China. Paper presented at ICSTLL-53, University of North Texas, October 2020. 7 pp.
tone_statements.quote: Fieldwork data reveals that Naruo has a syllable template of (C)(C/G)V(n) plus tone. ... As mentioned previously, due to the lack of phonetic data on Naruo at this time, this paper will not attempt to analyze Naruo’s tonal inventory in any detail. Available data suggests Naruo has at least four tones: high-level [55], mid-level [33], rising [24], and falling [21/31/52].
tone_statements.locator: sec. 4 'Preliminary Phonological Sketch': first sentence, tone inventory
tone_statements.summary: Preliminary sketch: 'at least four' tones (2 level, rising, falling with variants 21/31/52), count is the author's floor; tones assigned by comparison with Central Ngwi/Proto-Ngwi categories (sec. 3), not measured.

sources.citation: Yang, Cathryn; Kwok Wailing 范秀琳; Zhou Decai 周德才; Yang Wenjing 杨文静. 2017. 滇西北彝语他留土语群：忠诚的南诏战士 / The Taloid cluster of Northwestern Yunnan: Loyal Soldiers of the Nanzhao Kingdom. Presented at ICSTLL 50, Beijing. 8 pp. (slides, Chinese). Read as the academia.edu page text captured by the the Internet Archive (2025-05-15); the PDF itself is login-gated.
sources.note: Nothing. Historical-dialectology slides: lists 纳若 (水田) as Taloid member no. 5 (data from 2013 fieldwork), gives shared Taloid innovations (*a > u, *ak > a̱, *(-)rwe > ua), tone reflexes and lexical innovations; no mention of stress/重音/韵律.

sources.note: Naluo mentioned only when reviewing Bradley 2007's inventory (pp. 52-53); Lavu (Yongsheng) is used to represent the Talu/Shuitian/Zhili/Luo/Ziyi group; no Naluo profile and nothing on stress.

sources.note: Applies the Tonal Comparative Method (Dockum 2019) to ~200-word lists of 23 Ngwi languages (21 Central Ngwi; ~130 cognate sets; tone-onset correspondences sorted in Python) to test Bradley's (1977) Central Ngwi tone changes. Naruo (Foley 2020, own fieldwork) is one of five Taloid data points (Talu, Lavu, Kuansi, Naruo, Tagu); results are per cluster, not per language. Table (3) 'PN tone correspondences in six proposed clusters of CN' — Taloid column, recovered from the text by word x-position: *1 (high, modal) > 55; *2 (low, breathy) > 21~31; *3 (mid, creaky) > 33; *H (mid, tense/stopped) > 3…

sources.citation: Foley, Sean. 2022. The acoustics of apical vowels in two endangered Ngwi languages. Proceedings from the Annual Meeting of the Chicago Linguistic Society 57(1) [CLS 57, May 6-8, 2021, virtual], article 7. Chicago: Chicago Linguistic Society. (Published version on Ingenta Connect, pcls/2022/57/1/art00007, pagination not seen; author's open copy, 17 pp.:https://sfoley3.github.io/files/cls_57_foley.pdf.)
sources.note: Acoustic study of apical vowels, not of tone; contains no explicit tone inventory. Section 2.3 'Phonological sketch of Naruo and Lavu' covers sibilants and vowels only. All Naruo forms (Table 3 and the stimulus appendix, ~25 items) are transcribed with Chao tone letters showing three pitch values 55, 33 and 21 (e.g. ɕi²¹pu⁵⁵ 'Han Chinese', sɿ̠³³ 'firewood', ʂʅ²¹ 'seven', tsʰɿ⁵⁵ 'ten') plus an underlined (tense) vowel, i.e. Naruo is treated as a lexical-tone language with at least high-level, mid-level and low(-falling) tones; p.2 notes apical vowels 'can host lexical tone contrasts'.

tone.quote: Data used in the study came from fieldwork carried out on two endangered Ngwi languages spoken in Yunnan province in southwestern China, Naruo and Lavu. Naruo and Lavu are both grouped into Central Ngwi (Foley 2020) and both languages are still relatively under-documented. [...] Target segment Naruo Lavu / [i] ɕi²¹pu⁵⁵ ‘Han Chinese’ ɕi²¹ ‘new’ / [ɿ] sɿ̠ ³³ ‘firewood’ sɿ³³ ‘bowl’ / [ʅ] ʂʅ²¹ ‘seven’ ʂʅ³³ni³³ ‘day before yesterday’ / Table (3). Example lexical items used in the study.
